rot.segunda.demos.caca.1: Attack demonstration: the rook has left the king and gone to c1. Far from its protection, it is exposed to a queen fork. How do you get there?
rot.segunda.demos.caca.10: The queen captures the rook: the rook is won.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.2: Check on e4, along the diagonal to b7. The queen also watches b1: the rook loses its check along the b-file.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.3: The black king goes to c8, heading for the centre, where it has more squares.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.4: Your king steps up to b6 and shuts b7 and c7.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.5: The black king keeps heading for the centre and goes to d7.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.6: Check along the d-file: the black king must leave it.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.7: The black king goes to e6, away from your king.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.8: Fork: check on e3, along the e-file, and an attack on the rook on c1, along the diagonal.
rot.segunda.demos.caca.9: The black king steps out of check, and nothing protects the rook.
rot.segunda.demos.cravada.1: Attack demonstration: the rook on d7 is next to the king, which protects it. Your king is already close; what is missing is a queen move that wins the rook.
rot.segunda.demos.cravada.2: Pin: on f5, the queen pins the rook to the king on c8. Had your king gone to b6, the rook would check on d6, and capturing it would stalemate the king.
rot.segunda.demos.cravada.3: The black king goes to b8 and breaks the pin, but leaves the rook unprotected. On d8, it would be mated on the eighth rank.
rot.segunda.demos.cravada.4: The queen captures the rook: the rook is won, and the black king still has a8, so it is not stalemate.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: the black rook is on e7, on Black's second rank, the seventh rank of the board, near the king. This is the second-rank defence: the rook shuts b7, c7 and d7 to your king.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.e2: The plan: bring your king closer with the help of queen checks and, with the queen not giving check, take away the rook's checks. That keeps the black king stuck on the edge.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l1: Check on f5, along the diagonal to c8. The black king must respond, and your king gains time to come closer.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l10: The rook goes to c7, next to the king, which protects it again.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l11: The queen takes the eighth rank without giving check: the black king loses a8, b8 and c8 and only has a7.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l12: With the king almost out of squares, the rook leaves the king and goes to c1, to give checks from afar. It is the most stubborn defence.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l2: The black king goes to d8 and protects the rook on e7. The other replies lose much faster.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l3: Your king comes closer via c5, heading for c6 and d6, in front of the black king.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l4: The black king leaves the eighth rank and goes to c7, facing your king: it shuts b6, c6 and d6. But the rook on e7 is left unprotected.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l5: The queen goes to d5 without giving check: it watches e5, where the rook would give check, and takes b7, c6 and d7 from the black king. The rook has no checks.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l6: The rook goes to d7, next to the king, which protects it, and attacks your queen.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l7: The queen leaves the attack with check on e5, along the diagonal to c7.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l8: The black king steps out of check to b7. The rook on d7 loses the king's protection.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex1.l9: Your king goes to b5, in front of the black king, and shuts a6, b6 and c6: the black king is stuck on the last two ranks.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: another second-rank defence, with the rook on c7. The queen on e5, your king on d6 and the rook stand on the diagonal to b8: if the rook leaves c7, your king steps off the diagonal and the queen checks along it, a discovered check.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.e2: With Black to move, it would be zugzwang: every black move worsens the position. As it is your move, the queen makes a queen triangle and hands the move back.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l1: The queen drops back to f4, on the same diagonal: it is the first side of the triangle, from e5 to f4, then to f5 and back to e5.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l10: Forced move: the black king returns to b8.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l11: The queen goes to a5: this is Philidor's position, with Black to move. As you have already seen, the rook cannot escape.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l2: The black king goes to c8 and keeps protecting the rook on c7.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l3: Check on f5, along the diagonal to c8: it is the second side of the triangle.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l4: The black king returns to b8, next to the rook. The other replies lose faster.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l5: The queen returns to e5 and closes the triangle: it is the starting position, now with Black to move.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l6: In zugzwang, the rook goes to b7, still protected by the king. Every move loses; this one resists the longest.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l7: Discovered check: your king steps to c6, the queen on e5 gives check on b8, and the king attacks the rook on b7.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l8: The black king steps out of check to a7 and keeps protecting the rook.
rot.segunda.ideia.ex2.l9: Check along the a-file: the black king only has b8.
rot.segunda.pratica.canto.err.c2c7: On c7 the queen stands on the seventh rank, within the rook's reach, and the rook captures it.
rot.segunda.pratica.canto.err.c2f2: On f2 the queen stands on your king's file: the rook checks on f7 and, with the skewer, captures the queen.
rot.segunda.pratica.canto.err.c2g2: On g2 the queen stands on the rook's file, and the rook captures it.
rot.segunda.pratica.canto.fim: Rook won: the second-rank defence has fallen.
rot.segunda.pratica.canto.p: Attack: play White and win the rook. It is on the second rank, glued to the king in the corner: use the checks to bring your king closer and the queen to take away the rook's checks.
rot.segunda.pratica.fins.afogado: Stalemate: draw. Before each queen move, check which squares the black king has left.
rot.segunda.pratica.fins.limite: The move limit ran out before you won the rook. Use the checks to bring the king closer, not to push the black king from side to side.
rot.segunda.pratica.fins.repeticao: The position was repeated three times: draw. With each check, bring the king closer, without going back to the same position.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.err.c3c6: With the queen on c6, on your king's rank, the rook checks on f6: the skewer trades the rook for the queen, and it is a draw.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.err.c3c7: On c7 the queen stands on the seventh rank: the rook captures it, your king captures the rook, and it is a draw.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.err.c3f3: On f3 the queen stands on the rook's file, and the rook captures it.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.err.c3f6: On f6 the queen stands on the rook's file, and the rook captures it with check.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.err.c3g7: On g7 the queen stands next to the black king, which captures it.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.err.c3h8: On h8 the queen stands next to the black king, which captures it.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.err.d6c5: With your king on c5, on the queen's file, the rook checks on c7: the skewer trades the rook for the queen, and it is a draw.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.fim: End of the chapter: against the second-rank defence, checks to bring the king closer, the queen against the rook's checks and, in the end, the rook is won.
rot.segunda.pratica.lado.p: Attack: play White and win the rook. It is the same defence, now with the black king on the eighth rank. If the rook leaves the king, use the queen checks until the fork.
